questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It is a mix of many things. I have always had a connection to Italy, and I have for a long time had a great wish to experience living in the country and experience day to day life there. I had also conducted a lot of research on Italian universities and the courses they are offering, and Luiss' courses seemed very exciting and relevant.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university, Luiss, did a great job delivering the necessary information about introduction week, classes, exams etc. What goes for the Italian authorities, e.g. in terms of attaining the obligatory fiscal code, the information was very scarse.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was sufficiently assisted about introduction week, classes, exams etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Due to Luiss' housing service, Casa Luiss, it was very easy to find off campus housing as the university assisted me in finding accommodation. However, the communication was at times very frustrating.

I recommend reaching out to them as soon as possible to increase chances of finding accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Most of the time, you will need to get an Italian fiscal code. You most likely will not get it through the official Italian agency. Instead, if you are Danish, write to the Italian consulate in Copenhagen and ask for it. It is a hundred times easier. 

If you are going to Rome, it is not necessarily better to live in the city center as opposed to living closer to the university or in a nicer area such as Trieste.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive guidance in this matter via mail in proper time. However, some steps in this guiding framework are absolete and can therefore cause some confusion.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online guiding materials.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull - I got all the classes I signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready and fully clarified about your choice of classes on the registration day. It is first come first serve-princip.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The teaching methodology is different from University of Copenhagen and it is therefore difficult to compare the course level with that of Copenhagen. Yet, it is my only reference for elaborating the level of courses, and in that light, the level of courses were in generally not very high. The courses are in general less academic and more empirically based. This did, however, make the content of the courses seem quite basic.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was more centered around the professor and less around the academic literature - if there was any. In terms of engaging the students in the day to day teaching, it was similar to the UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Italian Foreign Policy
Geopolitics and Political Risk
Diplomacy and Negotiation
Energy and Climate Change Policy
The Politics of Cultural Heritage in Europe

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend History of Italian Foreign Policy, Energy and Climate Change Policy and The Politics of Cultural Heritage in Europe. Even though the teaching style in these courses were completely different,  and not necessarily very pedagogical, the content of the courses was interesting, and the atmosphere during the lessons was nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Weakly cleaning of the appartment as part of the contract without me knowing before arrival, very high extra costs to gas and heating during the winter months, acute plumbing service due to old toilet and a MR-scanning in a private clinic due to an accident.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarket prices was unexpectedly high (yet not higher than in Denmark) and heating and gas in the appartment very expensive. Going out for drinks and food can be much cheaper than in Denmark if looking in the right areas.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many. I don't know them all. I never attending the official activities because they acquired a health certificate, and I did not know how to get that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Attend the ESN football tournament if you like playing football. It is very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit some of the neighbouring towns, e.g. Tivoli, Anzio or Bracciano, or the countryside. Also, just explore Rome. You can easily spend half a year only exploring Rome itself.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Being to Italy many times before, it was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Share appartment with Italians, try to get to know Italians at the university (even though this can be more difficult than it sounds) and talk to the locals at bars.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food was very heavily pasta based, which is nice for some time but not for eternity.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How much life there always are on the streets and how outgoing the Italians are. There are going out more, but in a more relaxing fashion. That is fantastic.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Visit the coffee shops, visit the campus Villa Pola and enjoy the stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not necessarily better to live in the city center as opposed to living closer to the university or in a nicer area such as Trieste.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Simply living in Rome.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Communication with Casa Luiss.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
